learning_objective: 🎯 Master the art of effective communication, understand the communication cycle, overcome barriers, and learn how to provide constructive feedback in professional settings!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Communication is a continuous process involving a Sender (who encodes the idea), a Message, a Channel (medium), a Receiver (who decodes it), and Feedback (response confirming understanding).
Obstacles that distort the message: Physical barriers (noise, distance), Linguistic barriers (jargon, language difference), Interpersonal barriers (bias, poor listening), and Organizational barriers.
For any message to be effective, it must be: Clear, Concise, Concrete, Correct, Coherent, Complete, and Courteous.
Feedback completes the communication loop. Constructive feedback should be specific, timely, polite, and actionable—helping the receiver improve rather than feeling criticized.

fun_activity.title: 🤫 The Body Language Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Watch a 2-minute news clip or interview on mute. Try to guess the mood and relationship of the speakers purely by observing their facial expressions, hand gestures, and posture!

exam_tips: 📌 Always draw the circular flowchart of the Communication Cycle (Sender -> Message -> Channel -> Receiver -> Feedback) in exam questions.
📌 Memorize all '7 Cs of Effective Communication' with a one-line definition for each.
📌 Distinguish clearly between Verbal (spoken/written words), Non-verbal (gestures/body language), and Visual (charts/signs) communication.
quick_recap: ⭐ Non-verbal cues make up over 50% of the total impact of our face-to-face communication.
⭐ Active listening means fully focusing, understanding, responding, and remembering what is being said.
⭐ Descriptive feedback provides detailed guidance on what was done well and how to improve.
